text: 🇲🇽🌎 Mexico will not rush to congratulate Colombia's winner. "We will wait for the count to finish — this is a preliminary count. We wait for the final tally, which could arrive in August, and then we will congratulate whoever obtained the victory." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, asked about Colombia's election Standard 4T foreign policy: non-intervention, respect for the host country's own process. While other capitals — especially north of the border — rush to bless preferred candidates, Mexico waits for the institutions to do their work.

🇲🇽⚖️ Tomato down to 19.51 pesos/kilo. Diesel and gas stable. Weekly Profeco price report: tomato prices dropped sharply after recent spikes. Fuel prices held steady. Finabien — the federal Welfare Bank's remittance service — once again topped the ranking for lowest cost to send money home from the US. "El jitomate bajó a 19.51 pesos por kilo en promedio nacional." — Iván Escalante Ruiz, Procurador Federal del Consumidor Profeco publishes the comparison every Monday to put pressure on retailers and orient consumers. Finabien was built specifically to break the monopoly of private remittance giants.

🇲🇽✊ Beca Rita Cetina: 8,216,801 students covered. The Coordinación Nacional de Becas reported today that Mexico's universal primary-school scholarship now reaches over 8.2 million children. 2.1 million school supply cards have been distributed — 42% of the way to the July 31 target. Higher education's Jóvenes Escribiendo el Futuro covers another 479,031 students. "Cobertura: 8 millones 216 mil 801 estudiantes de educación básica." — Julio César León Trujillo, Coordinador Nacional de Becas para el Bienestar Cash transfers paid directly to mothers. No income screening, no merit test. Public school equals entitlement.

🇲🇽⚖️ "It's called democracy." "You can't talk about union democracy, not have the representation of the teachers of your section, and still want to remain the representative." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, on teacher union legitimacy Sheinbaum on the question of who really represents teachers inside the CNTE and SNTE: the answer is a vote of the rank-and-file. The 4T position is consistent — no charrismo, no imposed leadership. Legitimacy comes from the base.

🇲🇽⚖️ "That money does not go to the union. Ever." "These 800 million pesos have absolutely nothing to do with the CNTE. Nothing. They are not handed to the union for the union to give to schools. They are delivered directly to schools." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, on the SEP–CNTE agreement Opposition outlets framed last week's agreement as an 800 million peso 'bonus' to the dissident teachers' union in Oaxaca. Sheinbaum cut it down: every peso goes directly to schools — teacher positions, infrastructure, computers, uniforms, supplies. Federal money for kids, not for union leadership.

🇲🇽✊ "It's a matter of humanism — that the family be seen, who they are, their reality." Karla Ivette Gómez, a 48-year-old single mother and street vendor from the Centro Histórico, walked into Palacio Nacional with her two sons and Merlín — the duck who became the unofficial mascot of Mexico's 2026 World Cup team. "I've raised my three kids on my own. I feel honored to be Mexican. We are a working family. We are the beautiful part of Mexico." — Karla Ivette Gómez, at Sheinbaum's morning press conference The presidency frames it plainly: dignity for the family that sells in the street, not pity. Sheinbaum said the government will help convert the viral fame into improved quality of life.

🚨🇲🇽 "None. None. Absolutely none." Asked if her government worries about what 'El Mayo' Zambada might reveal to US authorities, Sheinbaum was unambiguous. AMLO's concern was never what the cartel boss could say — it was how a US agency removed him from Mexican soil. "If from the start a US agency or institution had planned it, there would have been a violation of sovereignty." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, responding to Ken Salazar's memoir Reforma published an excerpt of former US Ambassador Ken Salazar's book Borderlands claiming AMLO feared Zambada's revelations. Sheinbaum reframed it: the cooling of the AMLO–Salazar relationship was about sovereignty, not silence.

LATIN TIMES: Mexico Homicides Plunge to Historic Lows During 2026 World Cup Opening Days
June 19, 2026 | 🟢

📰 30 homicides the day Mexico played South Africa. 27 the following week. Down from 70+ per day at the start of Sheinbaum's term. Latin Times calls it "the Sheinbaum Effect."

Rare US-facing coverage that lets the numbers speak — no obligatory cartel paragraph for balance, no "but experts caution." Compare to the NYT's and WSJ's silence on the same data.

• "Mexico Homicides Plunge to Historic Lows"
• "the Sheinbaum Effect"
• 70+/day in Oct 2024 → 30/day during World Cup opener

NATIONAL REVIEW: Claudia Sheinbaum Leads Mexico into Confrontation
June 17, 2026 | 🔴

📰 Joshua Treviño (Texas Public Policy Foundation) argues Sheinbaum has put Mexico "on a collision course with both the United States and with basic Mexican democratic civics."

The opener invokes "April 19 deaths of two CIA officers in Chihuahua" — never officially acknowledged by Washington — as the precipitating crisis. The word "regime" does the rest of the work.

• "her government is on a collision course with both the United States and with basic Mexican democratic civics"
• "Mexico's regime is dragging it toward the abyss"
• "the damage done will take a generation to repair"

WSJ: Mexico Is Starting to Push Back Against Trump's Pressure Campaign
June 22, 2026 | 🟡

📰 WSJ confirms what Sheinbaum has been saying for months: Trump pressed her on a phone call to accept "a bigger role for the U.S. military" against cartels. She refused.

The headline almost reads as praise — until you notice the framing treats Mexican sovereignty as a "hardline stance" rather than the default position of any independent state.

• "Sheinbaum's hardline stance signaled that U.S. pressure for unilateral military intervention would put her and Trump on a collision course"
• Mexico refused to extradite indicted governor Rubén Rocha Moya
• 269 Mexican extradition requests still pending in US courts
